app.title: Beifahrer
status.title: Status
status.nobridge.title: No agent session running
status.nobridge.description: No agent can use a browser right now. Start an agent that has Beifahrer set up.
status.nobrowser.title: No browser connected
status.nobrowser.description: An agent session is running, but no browser is connected to it. Open the browser with the extension and check the pairing token.
status.ready.title: Ready
status.ready.description: An agent session is running and a browser is connected.
sessions.title: Agent sessions
unreadable: {count} registry files could not be read.
pairing.title: Pairing token
pairing.description: Paste this token into Beifahrer's settings in each browser, once. It lets the extension talk to the agent sessions on this computer.
pairing.other.title: Another token file exists
pairing.other.description: {path} holds a different token. A browser paired with that one cannot connect: paste the token above instead. An older Beifahrer that is still running may use the other one until it is restarted.
pairing.error: The token could not be read: {reason}
foreign.one: Port {ports} is held by something that does not report
foreign.many: Ports {ports} are held by something that does not report
foreign.description: No running agent session announced it. It may be an older Beifahrer, a bridge that no longer answers, or another program. A browser tries it like any other port. If it is a Beifahrer, restart the agent session that started it.
agents.title: Connect an agent
agents.description: Pick the app you use and paste the snippet into its MCP configuration.
agents.write.title: Allow filling and clicking
agents.write.subtitle: The agent may fill in forms and click on pages. Without this it can only look.
agents.nofile: No fixed file: see the agent's documentation
agents.checked: Checked against the agent's documentation on {date}. If it no longer works, follow the link.
agents.note: Which sites the agent may reach, and whether the browser asks before a change, you set in the extension. --allow-write only lets the agent try.
agents.nobridge: Beifahrer's bridge was not found in the usual place, so the command below is a placeholder. Install the bridge, or replace the command with the full path of beifahrer.
background.reason: Show whether your agent and browser are connected while the window is closed.
setup.agent.description: Pick the app that should use your browser. What was found on this computer comes first.
setup.config.backup: Before anything is changed, the old file is copied next to it with the time in its name.
setup.config.create.title: This file will be created
setup.config.create.description: The file does not exist yet. This is what would be written.
setup.config.update.title: This is what would change
setup.config.update.description: Only the Beifahrer entry is added or changed. Lines starting with + are new, lines starting with - go away.
setup.config.unchanged.title: Already set up
setup.config.unchanged.description: {name} already starts Beifahrer the right way. Nothing needs to be written.
setup.config.unparseable.title: The file is left alone
setup.config.unparseable.syntax: The window cannot read this file as plain settings, for example because it holds comments. It is not changed. Add the snippet by hand.
setup.config.unparseable.shape: This file is laid out in a way the window does not dare to change. It is not changed. Add the snippet by hand.
setup.config.unparseable.numbers: This file holds very large numbers that rewriting could round. It is not changed. Add the snippet by hand.
setup.config.unreadable.title: The file could not be read
setup.config.unreadable.description: It is not changed: {reason}. Add the snippet by hand.
setup.config.sandbox.title: This app cannot reach the file
setup.config.sandbox.description: Beifahrer runs in a sandbox here and cannot see your agent's settings. Add the snippet by hand.
setup.config.nofile.title: No fixed file
setup.config.nofile.description: The agent's documentation names no user file for this system, so the window writes nothing. Add the snippet where the documentation says.
setup.apply.written: Done. The old file was copied to {backup} first.
setup.apply.unchanged: The file already had this entry. Nothing was written.
setup.apply.notconfirmed: Nothing was written, because it was not confirmed.
setup.apply.changed: The file changed since you looked at it. Nothing was written. Go back one step and look again.
setup.apply.unparseable: The file cannot be rewritten safely. Nothing was written. Add the snippet by hand.
setup.apply.backupfailed: No backup could be made, so nothing was written: {reason}
setup.apply.writefailedbackup: Writing failed: {reason}. The old file is still in {backup}.
setup.browser.title: Your browser
setup.browser.description: The extension is Beifahrer's half inside the browser.
setup.browser.none: No browser was found automatically. Pick the one you use.
setup.extension.nostore: No browser store lists the extension yet, so it comes from the release on GitHub. The window itself downloads nothing: you open the link in your browser.
setup.extension.firefox.title: Firefox
setup.extension.firefox.body: Firefox installs the signed file in one click and updates it by itself afterwards.
setup.extension.firefox.step1: Click the button. Firefox opens and asks whether to add Beifahrer.
setup.extension.firefox.step3: Allow the extension to run in private windows only if you want that.
setup.extension.chromium.title: Chrome, Chromium, Brave and Edge
setup.extension.chromium.body: These browsers load the extension from a folder, because no store carries it yet. The download is a zip with that folder.
setup.extension.chromium.step1: Download the zip and unpack it somewhere you will keep it.
setup.extension.chromium.step2: Open the browser's extensions page (chrome://extensions, or edge://extensions) and switch on Developer mode.
setup.extension.chromium.step3: Choose Load unpacked and pick the unpacked folder.
setup.extension.chromium.step4: Do not delete the folder: the browser reads the extension from it.
setup.pairing.description: The extension needs the token below once. In your browser, click the Beifahrer icon in the toolbar and choose Settings (Chrome, Edge and Brave: first the puzzle icon, then Beifahrer). Paste the token there and come back.
setup.pairing.donetoast: Paired. Open Status to see the connection.
autostart.title: Start Beifahrer when you log in?
autostart.body: Beifahrer then waits quietly in the background and shows whether your agent and browser are connected. You can change this later under Preferences.
autostart.reason: Start Beifahrer in the background when you log in.
autostart.row.title: Start at login
autostart.row.subtitle: Beifahrer waits in the background and shows whether your agent and browser are connected.
autostart.failed: This could not be changed. Your system did not allow it.
setup.config.guide.title: Set up {name} in its own settings
setup.config.guide.description: This app is set up on its own screens. Beifahrer writes nothing here. Follow the steps and then continue.
guide.where.jan: Open Jan, go to Settings, then MCP Servers, and press the plus button.
guide.where.goose: Open Goose, go to Extensions and choose Add custom extension.
guide.where.cherry-studio: Open Cherry Studio, go to Settings, then MCP, then MCP Servers, and press Add.
guide.where.jetbrains: In your JetBrains IDE open Settings, then Tools, then AI Assistant, then Model Context Protocol (MCP), and press Add.
guide.where.other: Open the settings of your app and look for MCP servers. Some apps call them tools, connectors or extensions. The app has to support them.
guide.fields.kind: Choose a local server that runs on this computer (sometimes called stdio).
guide.fields.name: Name it beifahrer.
guide.fields.save: Save, then switch the server on.
guide.json: If the app wants JSON instead, paste the snippet below.
guide.json.paste: Paste the snippet below. Its name is beifahrer.
guide.flatpak: Beifahrer runs as a Flatpak here, so the command starts it through flatpak run. Your app must be allowed to run it.
guide.sandbox: If your app is itself a Flatpak or Snap, it may not be able to start programs outside its sandbox. Then put flatpak-spawn --host in front of the command.
diagram.fix.nobridge: Set Beifahrer up in your AI app, then start it.
diagram.fix.stalled: Your AI app started Beifahrer but never answered. Restart it, or set Beifahrer up again.
diagram.fix.nobrowser: Open your browser and enter the pairing token.
diagram.fix.partial: {name} is disconnected. Open it and pair it again.
diagram.fix.unreadable: A session file could not be read, so this may be out of date.
setup.extension.safari.title: Safari
setup.extension.safari.body: The extension comes with the Beifahrer app, so there is nothing to install. Turn it on in Safari's Settings, under Extensions, if you want to use Safari.
setup.extension.store.body: The extension is installed from the store, in the browser you picked.
setup.extension.store.step1: Add Beifahrer on the page that opens.
browser.list.title: Browsers
browser.list.description: Whether the extension is in each browser, and whether it is connected.
setup.extension.openfailed: The link could not be opened. Open it in your browser by hand.
safari.title: Safari (optional)
safari.hint: The extension comes with Beifahrer. Turn it on in Safari's Settings if you want to use Safari, then pair it with the token on this page.
